text: Turn an idea into something you can see, edit and discuss.
Start with a question, an existing artifact, or a direction you can't quite describe.
Ask for a useful study. See what feels right. Keep the source open for revision.
A publication cover turns a theme into type, color and a relationship between shapes.
A responsive website carries the same intent into layout, interaction and a smaller screen.
An identity study tests a mark, its variations, and an event poster in the same visual language.
A wayfinding study makes destinations and directions visible. Real-world use needs its own checks.
Run the included composition example, then use the optional helper to export a PNG.
The clean SVG stays editable. A companion guide view makes the layout choices inspectable.
Keep earlier studies. Compare their choices. A later revision isn't proof of a better design.
Say what to keep and what to change. A choice belongs to this study, not to a permanent taste score.
Explore the editable examples. Bring a question. Develop a direction with Ingenium.
